title: A hardcoded retired-owner list erases 2 of 10 2024 franchises from every public all-time aggregate, and 3 of the 10 all-time records on /league?tab=records name the wrong number and the wrong holder
subsystem: Public league — records / history / streaks / luck
claimUnderTest: src/public_league/identity.py:31-35 asserts that retiring an owner is cosmetic: 'Game-data references to their old roster slots (matchup results, trades) that exist in the Sleeper archives will simply attribute to "" and get filtered out by the same orphan-roster handling that skips un-assigned rosters, so no historical rewrite is required.' src/public_league/streaks.py:15-22 and records.py publish those aggregates as 'all-time'.
observed: The two retired owner_ids (714976074907336704 'Bwalk903', 720849338183548928 'SheriffB') held rosters 9 and 10 of the 10-roster 2024 league. metrics.resolve_owner returns '' for them, and every section does `if not owner_id: continue`, so 34 of 170 scored 2024 roster-weeks (20%) never enter the aggregates. Running the repo's OWN records.build_section with _RETIRED_OWNER_IDS emptied changes 5 of 10 record categories; 3 of them change at rank #1. This is not cosmetic and it IS a historical rewrite.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python /tmp/w19_retired2.py   # source archived at docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W19/retired-owner-diff-full.json; rebuilds the live snapshot twice, once with src.public_league.identity._RETIRED_OWNER_IDS = frozenset()
reproduction.expected: Identical record boards — the retirement list is documented as display-only
reproduction.actual: changedCategories = [singleWeekLowest, narrowestVictory, fewestPointsInWin, longestWinStreaks, longestLossStreaks]; history 2024 standings rows 8 -> 10; hallOfFame 12 -> 14; luck.byOwnerCareer 10 -> 12; streaks.currentStreaksByOwner 12 -> 14

numericProof.formula: records.build_section(snapshot) with vs without identity._RETIRED_OWNER_IDS; compare rank-1 value per category

userImpact: A visitor reading the public Records board is told the all-time lowest single-week score is 177.25 (it is 164.79), the all-time fewest points in a win is 241.23 (it is 236.61), and that the 2nd-longest win streak in league history (6) is held by Brent alone (SheriffB is tied at 6). They will cite these as league facts and settle arguments with them. The History tab shows an 8-team standings table for a 10-team season with no note.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding in the A21 Public League set covers the retired-owner filter. PRIOR-A21-F04 is a different erasure mechanism (0.00-point weeks in luck.py).

whatWorks: The values that ARE published verify exactly against Sleeper: records.singleWeekHighest[0] = 489.2 matches /league/1180092661344120832/matchups/15 roster 9 to 0.01. The defect is omission, not arithmetic.
rootCause: identity._RETIRED_OWNER_IDS strips the owners from the ManagerRegistry, which is the roster_id -> owner_id map every section resolves through. Filtering identity and filtering game data were conflated.
requiredRepair: Keep retired owners in roster_to_owner (so historical rows resolve) and filter them only at the display surfaces that need it (franchise dropdown, manager list). Alternatively stamp an explicit `excludedOwnerCount` / `historicalCoverageIncomplete` field on every section that drops rows and render it.

title: The public history payload self-contradicts: 2024 carries numTeams:10 and exactly 8 standings rows, and the History tab renders the 8-row table with no caveat
claimUnderTest: history.build_section emits a per-season block with numTeams and a standings array; frontend/app/league/sections/history.jsx:137 renders `(s.standings || []).map(...)` as THE standings table for that season.
observed: For 2024 the same object carries numTeams: 10 (read straight off the Sleeper league) and standings: 8 rows. Nothing reconciles the two and nothing renders numTeams, so the page shows an 8-team league standings table for a season Sleeper says had 10 rosters. This is the payload-level signature of W19-F001 and is independently checkable without any Sleeper call.

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/history | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; [print(s['season'], 'numTeams', s['numTeams'], 'standingsRows', len(s['standings'])) for s in json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['seasons']]"
reproduction.actual: 2026 numTeams 12 rows 12; 2025 numTeams 10 rows 10; 2024 numTeams 10 rows 8

userImpact: The public History tab presents a 2024 final standings table that is missing 20% of the league. A reader counting places believes the last-place team finished 8th when it finished 10th.
rootCause: Same as W19-F001. numTeams comes from the raw Sleeper league object; standings comes from metrics.season_standings, which drops unresolvable owners.
requiredRepair: Either fix the resolver (W19-F001) or assert numTeams == len(standings) at build time and stamp a `standingsIncomplete` flag the UI must render.

title: Public trade letter grades silently drop 224 of 1,708 traded asset slots (13.1%) that the board cannot price — including 20 first-round-pick slots — and emit a confident 'Robbery'/'Fleeced' badge with no unpriced-asset disclosure anywhere on the payload or the page
claimUnderTest: src/api/public_activity_valuation.py:70 says 'Returns 0.0 when no board value is available, which activity.build_section treats as "cannot grade this asset"'. src/trade/finder.py sets the house standard by counting omissions in metadata.assetsUnpricedByBoard.
observed: sanitize_side_values keeps only strictly-positive values, so a 0.0 asset is dropped from BOTH the linear sum and the KTC value adjustment — it is treated as if it were never in the trade, not as 'cannot grade'. The grade is still emitted. Across the live 191-trade public feed 224/1708 asset slots price to 0.0: 156 pick slots and 68 player slots. 63/191 trades (33%) and 126/393 sides (32%) contain at least one. The dropped picks include 6x '2024 R1' and 14x '2025 R1' slots — first-round rookie picks that were the headline asset of their trade. No field on the payload and no element on activity.jsx records the omission.

reproduction.expected: Either every traded asset carries a value, or the grade is suppressed / annotated when one does not
reproduction.actual: tradeGradeZeroPricedAssets = {totalByKind:{player:1238,pick:470}, zeroByKind:{pick:156,player:68}, tradesAffected:63/191, sidesAffected:126/393}; zeroPickLabels includes '2024 R1':6, '2025 R1':14, '2027 R5':6, '2029 R4':6

numericProof.formula: gotValue=sum(positive values); netAdjusted = netLinear + vaNet; pctGap = netAdjusted / max(got,gave) * 100 -> band table

userImpact: On the public Trades tab, Jason is publicly graded 'D — Robbery' on transaction 1388782397222293506 while three of the five assets he received counted as nothing. A reader — including league members — treats the letter as a verdict on a manager's competence. 33% of the public trade history carries a grade computed on an incomplete asset set with no warning.

priorFinding.note: The specific mechanism the prior audit described (floor to 1.0, then pow(...,1.65)) is GONE — activity.py no longer computes the grade and _GRADE_ALPHA no longer exists. sanitize_side_values now drops zeros instead of flooring them. The defect class survives the rewrite: unpriceable assets still vanish silently and a confident grade is still emitted. Same relation applies to PRIOR-A21-F02.

whatWorks: The grading arithmetic itself reproduces exactly: recomputing feed[0] through trade_grading.grade_trade_sides against the live private contract returns the identical served grades (Jason D, Ed A+, pctGap -27.866/+27.866). The scale bug the prior audit found is genuinely fixed.
rootCause: The valuation callable conflates 'worth zero' with 'not on this board'. The 2026 board carries pick rows for 2026-2028 rounds 1-6 only; every 2024/2025 pick and every round >=5 future pick has no row, and dropping them is indistinguishable from a zero-value asset downstream.
requiredRepair: Have the callable return None for 'unpriced' and 0.0 only for 'genuinely worthless'. Count unpriced assets per side, stamp `unpricedAssetCount` on the side, and suppress the grade (or badge it 'partial') when a side has any. This is exactly the posture src/trade/finder.py already ships as metadata.assetsUnpricedByBoard.

title: Eight 2026 awards are manufactured from a season with zero scored games — 'Points King: Jason, 0.0 PF', 'Regular-Season Crown: Jason, 0-0', 'League MVP: Justin Jefferson, 0.0 VORP' — and the live Awards tab counts them into its 'N yrs' award-history badge
claimUnderTest: awards.jsx:333 renders 'Season complete' vs 'Season in progress' on the FEATURED card only, and the page correctly says '2026 hasn't started yet'. The implicit claim is that an unstarted season contributes nothing.
observed: The 2026 season block (seasonStatus 'in_season', Sleeper last_scored_leg = null, weeksPlayed = 0) still emits 8 awards, all with zero-valued evidence: manager_of_the_year (wins 0, losses 0, winPct 0.0, pointsFor 0.0), points_king (pointsFor 0.0), regular_season_crown (record '0-0'), top_offense (offensePoints 0.0), trader_of_the_year (pointsGained 0.0), best_trade_of_the_year (pointsGained 0.0), waiver_king (pointsGained 0.0, adds 0), and league_mvp (Justin Jefferson, vorp 0.0, starterPoints 0.0, gamesStarted 13). Six of the eight go to Jason purely because the all-zero sort has no tiebreak. The block also stamps hasPlayerScoring: true, which is false in substance — players_points exists but every value is 0. awards.jsx builds historyByKey by iterating EVERY season with no isComplete filter (:273), so histCount (:355) includes 2026: the rendered page shows 'POINTS KING 3 yrs', 'MANAGER OF THE YEAR 3 yrs', 'REGULAR-SEASON CROWN 3 yrs' against 'CHAMPION 2 yrs' and 'HIGHEST SINGLE-WEEK SCORE 2 yrs'. The league has had exactly 2 completed seasons.

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/awards | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; r=[s for s in json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['bySeason'] if s['season']=='2026'][0]; print(r['seasonStatus'], r['hasPlayerScoring']); [print(a['key'], a['displayName'], a['value']) for a in r['awards']]"   # and: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/w19_tabs.py
reproduction.expected: Zero awards for a season with weeksPlayed = 0, and histCount = 2 for every award that only exists in completed seasons
reproduction.actual: 8 awards emitted; rendered badges read 'POINTS KING 3 yrs' / 'MANAGER OF THE YEAR 3 yrs' / 'REGULAR-SEASON CROWN 3 yrs'

numericProof.formula: histCount = historyByKey.get(key).length over bySeason with no isComplete filter

userImpact: A visitor opening the Awards tab sees Brent credited as a 3-time Points King when he has won it twice, and the award-history modal lists a 2026 winner with 0.0 points for a season that has not been played. Managers will dispute a trophy count that the site invented.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A21-F20 notes awards have no calibration; this is a different defect — emitting winners from an empty season and counting them as history.

whatWorks: The featured-season card correctly picks 2025 and prints '2026 hasn\'t started yet'. Completed-season awards verify: awards 2025 highest_single_week 489.2 matches Sleeper exactly.
rootCause: Award builders gate on the presence of matchup rows, not on any of them being scored. hasPlayerScoring tests for a players_points dict rather than a non-zero total. The frontend history reducer has no season filter.
requiredRepair: Gate every season-scoped award on weeksScored > 0 (matchup_points > 0 for at least one entry), fix hasPlayerScoring to test the sum, and filter historyByKey on isComplete || weeksScored > 0.

title: Six user-facing public surfaces label the coverage window 'the last 2 seasons' while the live window is 3 seasons and the page header on the same screen says 'Last 3 dynasty seasons'
claimUnderTest: PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS was widened from 2 to 3 (sleeper_client.py:43, comment: 'Widened to 3 after the 2025 playoffs + 2026 offseason shipped'). The header component correctly renders 'Seasons: 2024–2026 · 12 managers · Last 3 dynasty seasons'.
observed: Six copy strings were not updated with the constant. The Trades tab renders 'Trade activity — 191 completed trades across the last 2 seasons' directly under a header that says 'Last 3 dynasty seasons'; the 191 trades are 2024:29 + 2025:124 + 2026:38, i.e. three seasons. Same contradiction on Headline records, Hall of Fame, Superlatives, the rivalry deep link and the player-journey deep link. Eight Python docstrings carry the same stale figure.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/w19_tabs.py  # then grep tab-probe.json for '2 seasons'; also: grep -rn '2-season\|last 2 seasons' frontend/app/league/
reproduction.expected: Every coverage label derives from league.seasonsCovered.length (3)
reproduction.actual: 6 hardcoded 'last 2 seasons' / '2-season window' strings render next to a header that says 3

userImpact: A reader concludes the public trade archive covers only 2024-2025 and that the 2024 rows they can see are out of scope, or that a 3-season record was set in 2 seasons. It also understates the site's own coverage.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding covers the same stale '2 seasons' figure but only in docs/public_league.md. It did not identify the six USER-FACING strings, which is the part a visitor actually sees.

whatWorks: The page header and the /api/public/league league block both report the window honestly (seasonsCovered = 3, 'Last 3 dynasty seasons').
rootCause: PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS is an env-overridable constant; every consumer copy string hardcoded the value it had at write time.
requiredRepair: Derive all coverage copy from league.seasonsCovered (already on every section response) instead of literals. Add a test that greps frontend/app/league for a hardcoded season count.

title: The Superlatives tab is computed exclusively from TODAY's 2026 rosters but is captioned 'across the 2-season window', and mixes that point-in-time snapshot with 3-season transaction counts in the same card
claimUnderTest: frontend/app/league/sections/superlatives.jsx:27 subtitle: 'Fun, public-safe roster-composition awards across the 2-season window'. src/public_league/superlatives.py:19 docstring: 'most_active — most trades + waivers in the 2-season window'.
observed: _roster_composition (superlatives.py:41-56) reads `snapshot.current_season.rosters` and nothing else — the qb/rb/wr/te/idp/rookies/rosterSize numbers on every card are a snapshot of the 2026 rosters as of the last refresh, with no historical component at all. The winner's rosterSize of 58 matches the live 2026 Sleeper roster exactly. The SAME card then prints trades:14 / waivers:32, which ARE multi-season counts. So one card mixes a today-snapshot with a 3-season aggregate under a label that claims a 2-season window. None of the three is what the caption says.

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/superlatives | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; w=json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['mostQbHeavy']['winner']; print(w)" ; curl -s https://api.sleeper.app/v1/league/1312006700437352448/rosters | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; print([(x['owner_id'], len(x['players'])) for x in json.load(sys.stdin) if x['owner_id']=='1208452010173538304'])"
reproduction.expected: Either a genuine multi-season roster-composition measure, or a caption that says 'current rosters'
reproduction.actual: mostQbHeavy winner rosterSize 58 == live 2026 roster size 58; caption says '2-season window'

userImpact: A reader takes 'Most QB-heavy across the 2-season window' as a historical roster-building trait when it is a screenshot of one week's roster. A manager who just traded for two QBs wins a two-year award instantly.
whatWorks: The composition counts themselves are accurate against the live rosters, and the two transaction counters are genuine multi-season aggregates.
rootCause: The section was written against the current-roster dump because Sleeper exposes no historical week-level roster endpoint at the season-summary level; the caption was never reconciled with what was actually implemented. (Note: week-level ownership IS available in the matchup rows and IS used by player_journey.py — see W19-F010.)
requiredRepair: Either relabel to 'current rosters' or rebuild composition from the week-level `players` list on matchup entries the way player_journey._scoring_summary already does.

title: Three of the eleven required public navigation surfaces do not exist: Money and Constitution have zero code anywhere in the repo, and there is no Standings tab; League Media ships renamed as two AI-article tabs
claimUnderTest: The required public navigation is: Home, Standings, Franchises, Awards, Draft, Trades, Records, Money, Constitution, History, League Media.
observed: frontend/app/league/tabs.js ships 21 tabs. Mapping against the requirement: Home = overview (present), Franchises = franchise (present), Awards = awards (present), Draft = draft (present, plus a separate draft-capital tab), Trades = activity labelled 'Trades' (present), Records = records (present), History = history (present). ABSENT: Standings — no tab and no section; per-season standings tables exist only nested inside the History tab, and there is no current-season standings view at all. ABSENT: Money — `grep -rni 'constitution|dues|payout|league fee|entry fee'` across src/, frontend/app/, config/ and server.py returns zero hits outside an unrelated 'residues' variable in playoff_odds.py. ABSENT: Constitution — same zero-hit grep. RENAMED: League Media -> the 'Previews' and 'Recaps' tabs (ArticlesSection). 14 tabs are not on the required list.

reproduction.command: grep -rni 'constitution|dues|payout|entry fee' --include=*.py --include=*.jsx --include=*.js --include=*.json src/ frontend/app/ config/ server.py | grep -v residues ; .venv/bin/python -c "import re;print(re.findall(r'key: \"([a-zA-Z-]+)\"', open('frontend/app/league/tabs.js').read()))"
reproduction.actual: 8 of 11 present (Home, Franchises, Awards, Draft, Trades, Records, History, and League Media under two other names); Standings, Money, Constitution have no implementation

numericProof.formula: count of required nav entries with a reachable surface

userImpact: A league member looking for dues/payout status or the league constitution finds nothing and has no signal that the site was ever meant to carry them. A member looking for current standings has to open History and read a per-season table.
whatWorks: All 21 shipped tabs render with real, non-empty content in a real browser (see W19-F015 artifact). The 8 required surfaces that do exist all work.
rootCause: Money and Constitution are manual/CMS-shaped content with no data source in Sleeper; they were never built. Standings was folded into History rather than given a tab.
requiredRepair: Add a Standings tab reading the existing history.seasons[].standings (blocked by W19-F002 for 2024). Money and Constitution need a new content store — the smallest correct version is two static JSON files under config/ plus two read-only sections.

title: The public playoff-odds Monte Carlo returns binary 1.0 / 0.0 probabilities for a season with zero games played, and the payload carries no marker that the owners were unsimulated
claimUnderTest: power.jsx:286-290 describes the endpoint as 'a 10,000-simulation Monte Carlo on the backend' whose 'probabilities visibly jitter between visits' — i.e. a genuine stochastic estimate.
observed: With weeksPlayed: 0 and every currentPointsFor 0.0, the live response gives exactly seven owners playoffProbability 1.0 and five owners 0.0 for 7 playoff spots. There is no jitter and no uncertainty: playoff_odds.py:639-642 substitutes a single-element pool [100.0] for owners with no scored weeks, and rng.choice over a one-element list is a point mass. numSims stays 10000 on the payload, and nothing marks the owners as unsimulated. The card is currently shadowed because useSettings.js:143 defaults useRosPowerRankings to true (LeagueClient.jsx:391 then renders RosPowerSection), but the /settings toggle at page.jsx:759 makes it one click reachable.

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/playoffOdds | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin)['data']; print('weeksPlayed',d['weeksPlayed'],'numSims',d['numSims'],'spots',d['playoffSpots']); [print(o['displayName'], o['currentWins'], o['playoffProbability']) for o in d['owners']]"
reproduction.expected: With 0 games played and 7 of 12 spots, every probability near 7/12 = 0.583
reproduction.actual: 7 owners at exactly 1.0, 5 owners at exactly 0.0

numericProof.formula: uninformative prior P(make playoffs) = playoffSpots / teams

userImpact: With the ROS power toggle off, a preseason visitor is told five managers have a 0% chance of making the playoffs before a single game is played.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced on the live endpoint. The prior finding described the flat-100 placeholder mechanism; this adds the live measurement (7x 1.0 / 5x 0.0 at weeksPlayed 0) and the reachability path through the useRosPowerRankings toggle.

whatWorks: scheduleCertainty ('posted'), weeksPlayed and weeksRemaining are all stamped honestly on the payload — the information needed to suppress the card is present, it is simply not used.
rootCause: A degenerate single-value sampling pool is used as a stand-in for an uninformative prior.
requiredRepair: When an owner has no scored weeks, sample from the league-wide historical score distribution (or mark the owner unsimulated and omit them), and stamp `simulated: false` on the payload so the card can suppress itself.

title: VERIFIED POSITIVE — the public trade grader now uses the canonical linear-ratio + KTC-value-adjustment formula, and its served grades reproduce exactly; the prior audit's alpha=1.65 threshold-mismatch defect is gone from the tree
claimUnderTest: PRIOR-A21-F01 / PRIOR-A03-F01: 'src/public_league/activity.py:118 total += pow(max(val, 1.0), _GRADE_ALPHA) with _GRADE_ALPHA = 1.65 (:49)' produces an alpha-transformed pct bucketed against linear-calibrated 3/8/15/25/40 cuts, so the same trade grades Fair on /trades and Robbery on /league.
observed: Neither `_GRADE_ALPHA` nor the pow() line exists anywhere in src/public_league/. Grading moved to src/public_league/trade_grading.py, whose header documents the 2026-08-04 fix (finding C3) and implements the linear-ratio-with-VA form pinned to the frontend by the shared fixture tests/fixtures/trade_grade_parity_cases.json. I independently recomputed feed[0] by calling trade_grading.grade_trade_sides on values from src.api.public_activity_valuation against the live private contract and got byte-identical results to the served payload.

reproduction.command: grep -rn '_GRADE_ALPHA\|1.65' src/public_league/ ; .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.'); from src.api.public_activity_valuation import build_valuation_from_contract as B; from src.public_league import trade_grading as T; v=B(json.load(open('/tmp/w19_contract_full.json'))); p=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W19/public-league-full.json')); tx=p['sections']['activity']['feed'][0]; sv=lambda L:[v(a) or 0.0 for a in L or []]; print([g['grade']['grade'] for g in T.grade_trade_sides([(sv(s.get('receivedAssets')), sv(s.get('sentAssets'))) for s in tx['sides']])], [s['grade']['grade'] for s in tx['sides']])"
reproduction.expected: No alpha constant in the public grader; recomputed grades == served grades
reproduction.actual: grep returns nothing; recomputed ['D','A+'] == served ['D','A+'], pctGap -27.866032581200038 / +27.866032581200038

numericProof.formula: netAdjusted = (got - gave) + vaNet; pctGap = netAdjusted / max(got,gave) * 100

userImpact: None — this is a fix confirmation. The remaining defect on this surface is the unpriced-asset drop (W19-F003), which is a different cause.

priorFinding.note: The code the prior audit cited no longer exists. Same relation applies to PRIOR-A03-F01 and PRIOR-A21-F18 (analyzeRawTrade docstring), whose cited quantity is now the one actually used.

title: VERIFIED POSITIVE — the week-level roster-ownership join the all-time claims require DOES exist and is used: records, awards and the player-journey page all attribute points via per-week starters/players, not current roster membership
subsystem: Public league — records / awards / player journey
claimUnderTest: The correct methodology for an all-time player claim is weekly player scores joined to WEEK-LEVEL roster ownership. If franchise player leaders were computed from CURRENT roster membership, every historical claim would be wrong.
observed: records._player_records iterates season.matchups_by_week, reads that week's `starters` list and that week's `players_points` dict, and resolves the owner from that week's roster_id — a true week-level join. awards uses the identical _starter_set pattern. player_journey._scoring_summary goes further and reads the week's full `players` list, so it separates started / benched / not-rostered per manager and renders an 'Ownership arc'. There are NO franchise player leaders anywhere — franchise.build_section emits no player-scoring block at all, so the failure mode the prompt guards against is structurally absent. The only current-roster read in an all-time-labelled section is superlatives (W19-F006).

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json,urllib.request; p=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W19/public-league-full.json')); [ (lambda x: (lambda m: print(pos, x['playerName'], 'pub', x['points'], 'sleeper', (([q for q in m if q['roster_id']==x['rosterId']][0].get('players_points') or {}).get(x['playerId'])), 'starter', x['playerId'] in ([q for q in m if q['roster_id']==x['rosterId']][0].get('starters') or [])))(json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(f\"https://api.sleeper.app/v1/league/{x['leagueId']}/matchups/{x['week']}\").read())))(rows[0]) for pos,rows in p['sections']['records']['playerRecords'].items() if rows]" ; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/league/player/6794
reproduction.expected: Every published player record matches that week's players_points value and appears in that week's starters
reproduction.actual: 8/8 positions match to 0.01 and all 8 are starters: QB Jared Goff 64.60, RB Jonathan Taylor 59.98, WR Ja'Marr Chase 66.90, TE Brock Bowers 48.18, K Brandon Aubrey 31.20, DL Myles Garrett 64.50, LB Fred Warner 59.50, DB Brian Branch 55.95. /league/player/6794 renders 'Ownership arc: Jason -> MaKayla -> Brent' with per-manager started/benched splits.

numericProof.formula: published points == sleeper players_points[playerId] for the stamped (leagueId, week, rosterId)

userImpact: None — this is the part of the public history that is genuinely sound.

priorFinding.note: Recorded as a verified negative: the prompt's primary suspected defect does not reproduce.

title: AUDITED — /api/public/league leaks no private valuation, recommendation or tactical field to an anonymous caller; the only private-derived output is the trade letter grade, and the real exposures are raw Sleeper league/owner IDs (contradicting CLAUDE.md) plus a 2.08 MB anonymous response whose only consumer is sitemap.js
claimUnderTest: public_contract.py enforces a recursive field-name blocklist so no private internal can leave the backend; CLAUDE.md states 'Frontend callers should use the stable key from /api/leagues, not raw Sleeper league IDs — no endpoint exposes raw Sleeper IDs to the UI.'
observed: Section census of the 2,081,957-byte anonymous response: 3 top-level keys (contractVersion, league 8,092 b, sections 2,275,972 b, sectionKeys) and 17 sections — history 18 KB, rivalries 50 KB, awards 66 KB, records 39 KB, franchise 68 KB, activity 331 KB, draft 155 KB, weekly 93 KB, superlatives 29 KB, archives 801 KB, luck 66 KB, streaks 23 KB, power 97 KB, matchupPreview 12 KB, weeklyRecap 408 KB, teamAssignment 11 KB, overview 8 KB. A recursive key scan for value/grade/score/dollar/price/rank/edge/proj/tier/confidence/recommend/target/buy/sell/surplus/market finds no private field: no rankDerivedValue, no canonicalSiteValues, no edge signals, no trade suggestions, no dollar values. The 294 `value` keys are award evidence objects and the 808 `grade` keys are the {grade,color,label} trade badge. VERDICT: no numeric private valuation leaves the backend. Two real exposures do: (1) league.rootLeagueId / leagueIds / currentLeagueId are raw Sleeper league IDs and every manager carries a raw Sleeper ownerId, served anonymously — CLAUDE.md's 'no endpoint exposes raw Sleeper IDs to the UI' is false for this route; (2) the aggregate is 2.08 MB to any anonymous caller and the only consumer in the tree is frontend/app/sitemap.js:72, which uses it solely for league.managers and sections.rivalries.rivalries — the /league page itself deliberately fetches per-section instead.

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league -o /tmp/pl.json -w '%{http_code} %{size_download} %{time_total}\n' ; .venv/bin/python -c "import json,re,collections; d=json.load(open('/tmp/pl.json')); c=collections.Counter(); w=lambda o:[w(v) or c.update([k]) for k,v in o.items()] if isinstance(o,dict) else ([w(i) for i in o] if isinstance(o,list) else None); w(d); print([k for k in c if re.search(r'rankDerived|canonicalSite|edgeS|tradeS|arbitrage|waiverGem|siteWeights',k)]); print(d['league']['rootLeagueId'], d['league']['leagueIds'])"
reproduction.expected: No blocklisted field; per CLAUDE.md, no raw Sleeper IDs
reproduction.actual: 200, 2081957 bytes, 0.066 s anonymous; zero blocklisted fields; rootLeagueId 1312006700437352448 and leagueIds [1312006700437352448, 1180092661344120832, 1090320428817592320] served anonymously along with 12 raw ownerIds

numericProof.formula: recursive dict-key scan of the anonymous payload against _PRIVATE_FIELD_BLOCKLIST plus a value/recommendation regex

userImpact: Low. A raw Sleeper league_id is a read capability on the public Sleeper API (rosters, transactions, drafts) for anyone who has it, so publishing it widens what a scraper can pull without the site. The 2.08 MB anonymous response is an unauthenticated amplification surface for a payload nothing in the product actually needs whole.

priorFinding.note: Recorded as a verified negative on the leak question, with two secondary exposures found.

whatWorks: assert_public_payload_safe runs on every section and aggregate response and the blocklist is genuinely clean on live data. src/api/public_activity_valuation.py correctly keeps the raw private numbers server-side and emits only the derived letter.
rootCause: The aggregate route predates the per-section split; sitemap.js was never migrated to the cheap endpoints.
requiredRepair: Point sitemap.js at /api/public/league/rivalries (50 KB) + any section header for managers, then either retire the aggregate or gate it. Separately, correct the CLAUDE.md sentence — the accurate claim is that /api/leagues does not leak Sleeper IDs, not that no endpoint does.

title: /api/public/league* accepts a leagueKey query parameter, silently ignores it, and stamps no leagueKey on the response — while CLAUDE.md lists it under 'League-aware endpoints (all stamp leagueKey on their response)'
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'League-aware endpoints (all stamp leagueKey on their response): ... GET /api/public/league/* (routes through _public_league_id() which reads the registry)'. The documented validation table says an unknown leagueKey must return 400 unknown_league.
observed: Both handlers take no Request and no leagueKey. `?leagueKey=bogus_league` returns 200 with the default league's payload rather than the documented 400 unknown_league, and no response key named leagueKey exists at any depth of either payload (top-level keys are contractVersion, league, sections, sectionKeys / contractVersion, league, section, data).

reproduction.command: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league?leagueKey=bogus_league' ; curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/overview?leagueKey=bogus' | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(list(d.keys()), 'leagueKey' in json.dumps(d))"
reproduction.expected: 400 unknown_league per the CLAUDE.md validation table, or a stamped leagueKey per the league-aware table
reproduction.actual: 200 with the default league's payload; leagueKey absent from the response

numericProof.formula: count of 'leagueKey' keys in the response

userImpact: A future multi-league caller that passes leagueKey to the public route gets the wrong league's history with a 200 and no signal. Today the site has one public league, so no user is affected.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced at runtime rather than by signature reading: the parameter is accepted (200) and silently discarded, which is worse than simply not being wired, because the documented 400 never fires.

whatWorks: _public_league_id() does read the registry for the DEFAULT league, so the single-league case is correct.
rootCause: The public routes were built before the league-aware resolver and were added to the CLAUDE.md table aspirationally.
requiredRepair: Either wire _resolve_league_for_request into both handlers, or remove the route from the CLAUDE.md league-aware table and reject an unexpected leagueKey with 400 instead of ignoring it.

title: 153 of the 191 trades in the public Archives are tagged with the season's team-less awards ('Rivalry of the Year', 'Top Fantasy NFL Team'), which belong to no participant in those trades
claimUnderTest: archives.build_section attaches award tags so a searcher can find, for example, every trade made by that season's Manager of the Year.
observed: archives.py:269 keys the tag lookup on (season, '') — a literal empty owner id. The only awards carrying ownerId '' are top_nfl_team and rivalry_of_the_year, which have no owner by construction. Result on live data: every archives trade tag is one of exactly two strings, each appearing 153 times, and neither describes the trade or its participants. No owner-specific tag ever attaches.

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/archives | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys,collections; c=collections.Counter(); [c.update(t.get('tags') or []) for t in json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['trades']]; print(dict(c))"
reproduction.expected: Owner-specific award tags on trades made by award winners
reproduction.actual: {'Rivalry of the Year': 153, 'Top Fantasy NFL Team': 153} — nothing else

numericProof.formula: count of distinct tag strings across archives.trades

userImpact: A visitor filtering the trade archive by tag gets 153 unrelated trades under a rivalry label and finds no way to locate an award winner's trades. Minor: the tag column is decorative in the current UI.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced on the live payload with counts (153/191, exactly two distinct tags).

whatWorks: The seasonResults and rookieDrafts archive rows carry correct per-owner tags; only the trades path uses the empty-string key.
rootCause: The second element of the tag lookup key is the literal empty string instead of each participant's ownerId, which is computed one function earlier as `owners`.
requiredRepair: Key on each participant ownerId and union the resulting tag lists.

title: The 'Previews' and 'Recaps' tabs present a single eight-month-old article pair (2025 Week 17, the only two files that exist) as the live media surface, with no AI attribution on the tab and no indication the current season has nothing
claimUnderTest: Two of the 21 tabs are dedicated to AI-written previews and recaps, and articles.jsx:6-10 says the section lands on 'whatever the cron most recently wrote'. The requirement asks whether AI-generated narratives are labelled as generated.
observed: `find exports/narratives -type f` returns exactly 2 files: 2025/week-17/preview-1.json and 2025/week-17/recap-1.json — one matchup of one week, for a season that ended in December. Both tabs render that pair under the headings 'Week 17 previews · 2025' and 'Week 17 recaps · 2025' with the subtitle 'Wednesday-morning previews. Tap a card for the full article.' — present tense, no note that this is the only content that has ever been generated and that the current 2026 season has none. LABELLING: the slate page (/league/articles/2025/17) does say 'written by Claude using live league data', and the single-article page prints 'Generated <date> — claude-opus-4-7'; the two /league TABS carry no AI attribution at all, so the two most-visited entry points to this content are unlabelled. /league/articles/2026/1 correctly renders 'No articles yet'.

reproduction.command: find exports/narratives -type f ; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/league/articles | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('total', d['total'], 'season', d['season'], 'week', d['week'])" ; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/w19_deep.py
reproduction.expected: Current-season articles, or an explicit stale/empty state on the tabs, and AI attribution wherever generated prose is shown
reproduction.actual: 2 files total (2025 wk17 matchup 1); both tabs render them as the current slate with no staleness note and no AI attribution; only the two /league/articles/* pages carry attribution

numericProof.formula: files on disk / (weeks with scoring x matchups per week)

userImpact: A visitor clicking Previews in August 2026 reads a December 2025 championship preview written in the future tense ('Aguilar erases the 18.43 by Sunday-night kickoff') with nothing saying it is eight months old, and with no indication a language model wrote it.

priorFinding.note: File count reproduced exactly (2). This adds the UI consequence the prior finding did not cover: the two tabs render the stale pair as current and carry no AI attribution, while the deeper pages do.

whatWorks: The /league/articles/[season]/[week] slate page and the single-article page both attribute the content to Claude and stamp the model id and generation time. /league/articles/2026/1 degrades honestly.
rootCause: Per PRIOR-A07-F15 the weekly-narratives workflow has never had an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and now green-skips. The tabs have no staleness threshold.
requiredRepair: Show the article date prominently on the tab card and render an explicit 'no articles for the current season' state when the newest group is not the current (season, week). Move the 'written by Claude' attribution into ArticlesSection so it appears on the tabs too.

title: VERIFIED POSITIVE — all 21 /league tabs and all 10 dynamic deep-link routes render real, non-fabricated content in a real browser, and every not-found path degrades with a specific honest message rather than a 404 or a blank
claimUnderTest: Every tab renders with real data; the dynamic routes work with real values.
observed: All 21 tabs loaded through Playwright with /api/* request interception (per AUDIT_PROTOCOL): every one returned non-empty content, none matched a no-data/empty/failed-to-load regex, and none showed fabricated placeholder rows. draft renders 512 table rows, history 46, rivalries 49, draft-capital 85. Archives initially looks stuck at 'Loading section...' — it is not broken, it is a 737 KB client-side lazy fetch that resolves in roughly 3 s and then renders 191/1092/158/494/30/968/12 rows across its seven kinds. Deep links: /league/franchise/468418790212759552, /league/player/6794, /league/rivalry/<a>-vs-<b>, /league/week/2025/17, /league/weekly/2025/17/1, /league/articles/2025/17 and /league/articles/2025/17/1/recap all render real content. Miss paths return 200 with a specific message, never a bare 404: 'Franchise not found — No public franchise record for owner <id>', 'Player not found — No public journey data for player 99999999', 'Recap not found — No recap for 2026 week 1 — the week may not be scored yet', 'No articles yet — Nothing has been generated for 2026 Week 1'. /league/insider-trading is a 307 to the login gate (private page, correct).

reproduction.expected: 21/21 tabs and 10/10 routes render content; miss paths degrade honestly
reproduction.actual: 21/21 tabs non-empty, 0 matched an empty-state regex; 13/13 probed deep-link URLs returned 200 with either real content or a specific not-found message

numericProof.formula: count of tabs whose rendered body text is non-trivial and does not match /no data|unavailable|failed to load/i

userImpact: None — positive result. The defects on these pages are in what the numbers MEAN (W19-F001..F008), not in whether they render.

title: Four of the seven public Archives tables render raw 18-digit Sleeper owner IDs where a manager name belongs — 1,441 of 2,035 archive rows
claimUnderTest: The Archives tab is captioned 'Full searchable history of trades, waivers, matchups, drafts, and season results' and its data carries a `managers` list (12 rows) with displayName for exactly this purpose.
observed: archives.jsx renders `{(r.ownerIds || []).join(' ↔ ')}` under the Trades table's 'Teams' column, `{r.ownerId}` under the Waivers table's 'Manager' column, and `{r.homeOwnerId}` / `{r.awayOwnerId}` under the Matchups table's Home/Away columns. The rendered page shows rows like '2026 1 468418790212759552 ↔ 711452264774041600 7 WR, WR, WR, WR'. The rookieDrafts, seasonResults and managers tables correctly show teamName / displayName, so the resolver is available and simply is not applied. Affected rows: 191 trades + 1,092 waivers + 158 matchups = 1,441 of 2,035.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/w19_archives.py   # wait 15 s for the 737 KB lazy fetch, then read the rendered table text

userImpact: The public Archives tab — the site's own 'full searchable history' — is unreadable for its three largest datasets, and the free-text search matches on the ID rather than the manager's name, so typing 'Jason' returns nothing in Trades.
whatWorks: The lazy fetch, kind switching, season filter and 500-row cap all work; the rookieDrafts / seasonResults / managers tables resolve names correctly.
rootCause: Three table renderers were written before the managers list was threaded into the section and never updated.
requiredRepair: Pass `data.managers` (already in the payload) through a nameFor() helper in all four cells, and include the resolved name in archiveSearchTokens.

title: 'All-time' league records are actually a rolling PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS=3 window; it is correct only by coincidence today and will silently start truncating history at the 2027 season with no label change
claimUnderTest: src/public_league/streaks.py documents longestWinStreaks/longestLossStreaks as 'top-5 all-time' and recordsInReach as 'per all-time record, the reigning holder'; _ordinal_label emits the literal string '<n>th-<thing> all-time' into the UI.
observed: snapshot.build_public_snapshot walks the Sleeper previous_league_id chain capped at PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS (default 3). The chain currently terminates on its own — GET /v1/league/1090320428817592320 returns previous_league_id '0' for the 2024 season — so the 3-season window happens to equal the league's entire life and 'all-time' is true by accident. Nothing detects that coincidence. When the 2027 league is created the walk will stop at 2027/2026/2025 and drop 2024 entirely, at which point every string containing 'all-time' becomes false and no code, label or test will notice. Neither the payload nor the UI carries a windowIsCompleteHistory flag, and seasonsCovered is the only signal — which the record cards do not render.

reproduction.command: curl -s --max-time 20 https://api.sleeper.app/v1/league/1090320428817592320 | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['season'], 'previous_league_id', d['previous_league_id'])" ; grep -n 'PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS' src/public_league/sleeper_client.py ; grep -n 'all-time' src/public_league/streaks.py
reproduction.expected: Either an uncapped walk for all-time claims, or a label that names the window
reproduction.actual: previous_league_id '0' (chain length 3 == cap 3, coincidence); PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS defaults to 3; streaks.py:371 emits '<n>th-<thing> all-time'

userImpact: None today (beyond W19-F001, which already makes 'all-time' false for a different reason). From the 2027 season onward every all-time record silently becomes a 3-season record and the 2024 champion disappears from the Hall of Fame with no notice.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding flags that docs/public_league.md states the wrong window size. This is the different and larger consequence: the cap silently invalidates the 'all-time' vocabulary, with zero headroom left.

whatWorks: seasonsCovered is stamped honestly on every section response and the page header renders it correctly ('Last 3 dynasty seasons').
rootCause: A performance cap on the Sleeper chain walk is being used as the domain of an all-time claim.
requiredRepair: Stamp `windowIsCompleteHistory` on the snapshot (true iff the chain terminated at previous_league_id '0'/null before the cap) and make every 'all-time' string conditional on it; otherwise render 'last N seasons'.
